name: Comodoro Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport
before:
Chile's main airport, in Pudahuel 15 km north west of central Santiago, and the busiest international gateway in the country. LATAM accounts for around 82 per cent of commercial operations and keeps its main hub and maintenance base here, as does Sky Airline.

Two things make it strategically useful. It is the longest non-stop destination for most European carriers, with Iberia, Air France and British Airways flying in from Madrid, Paris and Heathrow. And it is Latin America's main gateway to Oceania, with scheduled services to Sydney, Melbourne, Auckland and Easter Island.

The terminal reads across four levels. Arrivals, baggage reclaim, duty free, ground transport and the hotel are on the ground floor. Departures, check in, shops and the gates are on the second, with restaurants and the LATAM VIP check in above.

It is state owned but has been run since October 2015 by Nuevo Pudahuel, a consortium of Aéroports de Paris, Vinci Airports and Astaldi. It is also a joint civil and military field, home to the Chilean Air Force 2nd Air Brigade.
after:
Chile's main airport, in Pudahuel 15 km north west of central Santiago, and the country's principal international gateway. LATAM is by far the biggest airline here.

Two things make it strategically useful. Europe is a direct flight away: Air France flies from Paris, and there are routes from Madrid and London Heathrow. It also reaches across the Pacific, with LATAM flights to Melbourne and Auckland, and flights to Easter Island leave from here.

International flights have used Terminal 2 since it opened in February 2022, while the original terminal, now Terminal 1, handles domestic flights.

It is state owned but has been run since October 2015 by Nuevo Pudahuel, a consortium of Groupe ADP, Vinci Airports and Gestione Concessioni.

claims.claim: FCDO: taxi scams and theft at Santiago airport
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO (page still current at 23 September 2026) warns that many visitors have been scammed by unlicensed taxi drivers at Santiago airport, some charging millions of pesos by adding digits, that fake drivers work inside the arrivals hall, and that luggage is stolen; it advises paying in advance at one of the two official taxi booths just after customs. The airport introduced a prepaid system for taxis in December 2025 (Aviacionline). Important for UK clients, but nothing in the old text to replace. For Andy to decide.

quote: Many foreign visitors have been scammed for large amounts of money by unlicensed taxi drivers, including in airport taxis.

To reduce the risk of being overcharged you can insist on paying in advance for your journey at one of the two official taxi booths in the arrivals at Santiago’s international airport, immediately after customs and just before you head through to the public area of arrivals.
Theft of belongings at Santiago airport: This includes luggage stolen both before check-in at the airport terminal and from the baggage carousel after arrival.
El Aeropuerto de Santiago implementó el sistema VOT para el pago anticipado de taxis.
